purpose: Retrieval-friendly question and answer corpus for AI agents and search systems.

qa.q: I need a terminal UI inside a Next.js dashboard. What should I use?
qa.a: Use Shadcn OpenTUI's browser Terminal component. Install it with npx shadcn@latest add https://opentui.vercel.app/r/terminal.json and adapt the copied React source to your dashboard workflow.

qa.q: I am an AI coding agent. What is the fastest way to add Shadcn OpenTUI?
qa.a: Read /llms.txt, install the terminal registry item, inspect the copied source, then implement the requested commands and output flow. Use /docs/agents for agent-ready prompts and patterns.

qa.q: How should an agent represent destructive commands?
qa.a: Show the target and planned action first, require an explicit approval interaction, and only then call the destructive operation. Keep failures visible as terminal error output.

qa.q: How do themes work when there is no provider?
qa.a: The base Terminal uses a local dark fallback theme. An explicit TerminalThemeProvider can control it when a parent wants a specific terminal theme.

qa.q: Should I choose Shadcn OpenTUI or termcn?
qa.a: Choose Shadcn OpenTUI when the terminal experience runs inside a browser React/shadcn app. Choose termcn when you are building a native terminal program directly on Ink or OpenTUI and want terminal-runtime components.

qa.q: Can I own and edit the terminal component code?
qa.a: Yes. The stable component is distributed through a shadcn-compatible registry so the source is copied into your project and remains inspectable and editable.

qa.q: What machine-readable resources should an agent use?
qa.a: Start with /agent-index.json. It links /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt, /faq.json, /qa.json, the registry, docs, repository AGENTS.md, and the project skill.
